name: ambrotype
definition: a collodion positive image on a glass plate, backed with a dark ground so the negative reads as a positive.
reason: Sold under its own name; GA lists it as a process; no kind covers glass (tintype is iron, daguerreotype silvered copper).

name: lacquer painting
definition: an image built in layers of natural or synthetic lacquer on a rigid panel, sanded and polished, often with inlaid shell or metal leaf.
reason: Binder is the kind axis; no kind covers lacquer; own class at Singulart and Zhongyi (two regions, C11).
Memo section 7: street art and graffiti are a tag; spray-paint painting is the kind.
Gold or metal leaf is an added material or ground on a painting kind (C2(b)); where several media combine, F2.1.10.
Enamel paint is a paint type on an unchanged form (C10 retail facet). Fired vitreous enamel plaques not shown by the page; left for harvest.

name: embossed print
definition: an image made by pressing damp paper into a carved or built-up matrix so the design stands in relief, mainly without ink; embossing added to an inked print is an attribute.
reason: Process is the kind axis; AAT-PR lists embossed prints apart; Motokawa names the technique; no print kind covers inkless relief.

name: paper cut
definition: a picture made by cutting one or more sheets of paper so the image is formed by the cuts, mounted for display (jianzhi, Scherenschnitte, kirie as named forms).
reason: Image made by cutting, not pasting, so not collage; sold under its own name; pasted cut-outs stay collage F2.8.01.
Pasted photographs are collage by definition; a darkroom combination print is filed by its photographic process.
A digital print is an inkjet print (F2.3.6.01); a photograph printed in pigment is F2.4.3.01.
Key step 7: a taxidermy specimen is F6; animal parts combined with other materials stay F2.5.8.01 (precedence 10).
